answer: Cloned smelter badges were cashing pour-list pay as if each badge ran its own kiln. A worker now leases one kiln mouth bored through a named shale seam, hangs a ferrous coupon logged to 0.2 grams, and threads a living vine sensor so four heat traces, 16 minutes apart, open only with that coupon key. The lease withholds 6.4 coin-units for 44 hours. Jury clerks reweigh the coupon against the assay book and drop any kiln whose ferrous serial or vine trace appears on two pour lists. A coupon under two badges, or a heat trace that copies a parent hash, voids the withheld coins.
